transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa, Diego, Priya, Samir, Leah
Links: postmortem doc: https://internal.redwood/reports/2026-05-05-incident-postmortem.md; slides: /shared/launch-readiness/2026-05-05.pdf

Summary: Quick incident review after launch readiness failures in staging causing increased latency and some 5xxs. We go through timeline, RCA, mitigations, and rollout plan.

[00:00] Alyssa: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, this is the launch readiness incident review for the spike we saw on tuesday, um we've got the timeline in the doc, i think diego will kick off with the engineering summary?
[00:22] Diego: yeah thanks, so quick TLDR — during the large parallel load tests the inference service started to see pod OOMs around 09:10 which led to rolling restarts and temporary capacity loss, that in turn triggered our fallback to hosted model variants and some requests timed out, um initial traces point at memory growth in the token-merge path when batching increases, i will show a chart in a minute but basically the KV cache + bigger batch sizes seem to amplify mem usage
[00:50] Priya: and to add some context our autoscaler scaled but slower than expected because the CPU signal looked fine, memory wasn't the autoscaler input so pods hit OOM before new replicas were provisioned, so autoscaler config mismatch, also we saw kube evictions shortly after
[01:18] Samir: yeah i was looking at the heap dumps, there's a leak in the token merge buffer when sequences exceed ~2k tokens, the buffer isn't releasing on edge cases, it's a bug introduced in the refactor last month (PR #2784 maybe), so that explains the growth
[01:46] Alyssa: ok that explains the root cause hypothesis, does this match the postmortem doc timeline?
[02:03] Diego: yes, timeline on doc is slightly more detailed — we have the exact spike at 09:07, first pod OOM 09:10, fallback routing triggered 09:12, degraded latency until 09:47 when manual intervention reduced batch sizes
[02:30] Priya: we should call out that the KV cash (sic) warmup also bumped memory since cache entries were getting pinned longer during the stress test, so the combined effect was bigger than each alone
[02:58] Leah: for the launch checklist, we need a clear owner for the canary and for the customer comms, i'm happy to draft the incident note
[03:15] Diego: i can own the RCA doc and the patch PR, samir will lead the code fix, priya will own autoscaler changes and the load tests after patch
[03:40] Alyssa: good. on mitigation — we had two lines: immediate ops mitigation and longer term fixes; immediate was reduce default batch size and increase pod memory limit, long term is patch token merge leak and make memory a metric for autoscaler
[04:05] Samir: small note — the memory bump is most visible when KV caching is enabled with prefix reuse, if we disable prefix caching memory stays lower, but that has perf cost so we need a balanced solution
[04:30] Diego: Also worth noting the model variant fallback worked as designed — routing sent to a smaller quantized variant, that kept some requests alive but degraded quality; we should capture that in release notes as a known tradeoff
[04:56] Priya: ops question: do we have SLOs impacted? i think some customers in staging hit degraded latency but production was unaffected, we need to document thresholds and add alerts when memory per pod crosses 70% over 5m
[05:20] Alyssa: yes add that to the runbook, priya can you propose alert thresholds?
[05:35] Priya: yea i'll propose 70% and 85% critical, tie to pages to on-call if sustained 3 minutes
[05:52] Diego: another area — observability gaps, we missed a clear correlation between batch_size distribution and memory because we only sampled trace spans at 1% in staging; need to bump sampling during rollout windows or add a lightweight histogram metric for batch sizes
[06:14] Samir: agreed, adding a histogram for sequence length and batch size per request would have shown the correlation quickly
[06:32] Alyssa: ok so action items are clear, can we talk about rollout plan — we were supposed to canary model-client 2.1 next week, do we delay?
[06:50] Diego: prefer to patch and do a canary with the patch in staging first, if patch looks good, proceed with canary on prod with reduced batch config; we should automate rollback on OOM alarms
[07:10] Priya: ops side — i'll ensure the autoscaler uses memory as an input for the canary, plus provisioning faster scale-up windows for that zone, and i'll run a soak test after patch with synthetic traffic
[07:33] Leah: customer comms — we should be transparent but not alarm, a short note explaining that staging had degraded perf during tests, root cause and mitigation, and that prod unaffected, ready to publish once diego confirms RCA and samir confirms patch
[07:58] Diego: one more technical point — we saw cgroup memory vs container memory differences, some nodes had oom_killings at node level, so need to align kubelet and container limits, there was a mis-config in the Helm chart where requests/limits didn't match for the sidecar image
[08:24] Samir: yeah that was my bad, i missed the sidecar limit change during the last templating, i'll fix the chart and open PR, mention in the postmortem
[08:45] Alyssa: perfect. timeline for fixes? samir and diego have a patch + PR by 2026-05-09, priya does autoscaler update and load test by 2026-05-08, leah drafts customer note 2026-05-06
[09:05] Priya: on detection/alarms — we should create a memory spike alert and an aggregate ooms alert, plus a runbook link; runbook should include immediate steps to reduce batch size and scale down the request rate if rollback can't be immediate
[09:30] Diego: i also want to add a test in our CI that runs a memory stresser on the token-merge path for PRs touching that code, so we don't regress again
[09:50] Samir: i can add that as a unit/integration harness, maybe a dockerized memtest in CI with permissive thresholds for day-0 tests
[10:10] Alyssa: excellent. anything else on launch readiness aside from the incident?
[10:20] Leah: checklist items — confirm SOC2 audit artifacts for launch, ensure KMS rotation docs are up-to-date, update privacy page copy if needed, and ensure sales/SEs have the latest perf numbers
[10:41] Diego: perf numbers — we'll re-run benchmarks after patch but initial numbers look fine, latency  p50 54ms p95 320ms under normal load, spike pushed p95 above 1.2s during the incident
[11:00] Priya: also we should talk about routing policy: we fell back to hosted variant automatically, maybe we want a configurable fallback policy per-customer so enterprise customers can opt-out of lower-quality fallbacks
[11:25] Alyssa: yep add that as a product decision item for the roadmap — flag for Q3 maybe to support per-account fallback policy and stronger SLAs on routing
[11:45] Diego: ok final recap — owning items: Diego RCA and routing notes, Samir patch and chart fixes, Priya autoscaler and alerts, Leah comms and status update. We'll reconvene after PRs land or sooner if we find anything new.
[12:05] Alyssa: thanks everyone, i'll compile the notes and post the updated postmortem with action items, ping when the PRs are ready.
[12:20] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "ooms" typed lowercase, product name typed as "model-client" or "model client" in different parts. Speaker overlaps and quick interruptions are present.
